cohort: The study included deliveries from a 10-year hospital-based cohort (2008-2017) and a four-year case-control group (2008-2011) studying severe postpartum hemorrhage.
finding: The increased rate of severe postpartum hemorrhage observed during the study period was primarily due to an increase in uterine atony-related PPH, while PPH caused by retained tissue remained stable.
mod_finding: Operative delivery was identified as a risk factor associated only with severe postpartum hemorrhage caused by uterine atony.
